historical_references.reference: Xandiel was a legendary figure in the early Christian Church, believed to have been a hermit who lived in the Sinai Peninsula in the 5th century AD. He is said to have been a disciple of Saint Anthony the Great and is known for his extreme ascetic practices and miraculous deeds.

Another account suggests that Xandiel was a bishop in the 6th century AD in the region of Cappadocia, in present-day Turkey. He is known for his role in the Monophysite controversy, a theological dispute regarding the nature of Christ's divinity and humanity.
